questions.stem: How does acid rain damage limestone buildings?

options.text: The acid dissolves the paint on the buildings
The acid makes the building expand and crack
The acid reacts with calcium carbonate in limestone, dissolving it: CaCO3 + H2SO4 -> CaSO4 + H2O + CO2
The acid causes the building to rust

questions.explanation: Limestone is made of calcium carbonate (CaCO3). The sulfuric and nitric acids in acid rain react with calcium carbonate, dissolving it: CaCO3 + H2SO4 -> CaSO4 + H2O + CO2. This gradually erodes the surface, damaging carved details on historic buildings and monuments irreversibly.
